## Why visit

A memorable traditional stop for low beams, leaded windows, stone flooring and small rooms, with a strong sense of Bolton’s local history. Choose it for the atmosphere and surviving fabric rather than uncritically repeating claims about being Britain’s fourth-oldest pub. It is also a useful reminder that a historic cider reputation and present-day real-cider availability are different things. An earlier, quieter visit is likely to suit appreciation of the rooms; weekend bands can turn it into a much livelier venue. Combine with the Bank Top tap if local cask is the day’s focus.

## Beer

CAMRA records cask ale, commonly including local Bank Top beer.

## Cider and perry

**No real cider reported by the cited evidence.** Despite the Cider ’Ouse nickname, CAMRA’s June 2026 record says none of its current ciders meet the revised real-cider definition.
